Add initial values for nodes that JAGS >= 5 cannot initialise

Source: R/helpfunctions_model_imp.R
add_jags5_inits.Rd

JAGS >= 5 sets initial values that are not given from the prior (see rjags::jags.model(), argument initrep): for a bounded parameter, it takes the value with the highest prior density, for an unbounded parameter the mean of many draws from the prior. For some parameters of JointAI's models, these values are extreme, and the model cannot be initialised ("Node inconsistent with parents"):

  • The precision of random effects with a truncated gamma prior (see get_ranef_precision_nodes()) starts close to the lower bound 1e-16; the random effects then start at extreme values (e.g., in proportional hazards models or generalised linear mixed models).

  • The shape parameter of a Weibull survival model (see get_survreg_shape_nodes()) starts at about 100 (the mean of its prior); the survival time to the power of the shape then overflows.

Usage

add_jags5_inits(inits, nodes, seed, jags5 = rjags::jags.version() >= "5.0.0")

Arguments

inits

a list with one list of initial values per chain, as obtained from get_initial_values()

nodes

a named integer vector, as obtained from get_jags5_init_nodes(): per node the number of rows and columns of a precision matrix, or 0L for a single value

seed

an optional seed value, to draw the same values again

jags5

logical; whether the initial values are added (by default with JAGS >= 5)

Value

inits, with an initial value for each node that is not in the initial values of a chain (see draw_jags5_init())

Details

JAGS 4 started these models at values that worked (the random effects at zero, the shape at about 10), so nothing is changed for JAGS < 5.

The initial values are drawn per chain from a log-uniform distribution between 0.5 and 2 (so that the chains start at different values; for a precision, the variance then lies in the same range). Values the user supplied for a node are kept.
